title: The false self and the true self
hookLine: the self built on image and approval versus the self God knows

lines: THE VERSION OF YOU IN PUBLIC.
cards: There's a version of you that goes out into the world. The one in the profile picture, the one at work, the one at the family dinner. It's funny when it needs to be, busy, a little impressive.
It knows what to say. Keeping it polished takes energy. And late at night, a quiet question can slip in: is that actually me?
Thomas Merton spent years on that question.

teach.h: A SELF MADE OF IMAGE AND APPROVAL.
teach.b: First, the false self. In New Seeds of Contemplation, Merton says each of us is shadowed by an illusory person, a false self, built out of image, approval, achievement and possessions.
It wants to be seen, so it keeps wrapping itself in more things to be noticed.

teach.h: A BODY SEEN ONLY IN BANDAGES.
teach.b: Merton pictures it as an invisible body that can only be seen when it's wrapped in bandages. Unwind the bandages, and there's nothing there. Second, it isn't the body or the personality.

Merton isn't saying your talents or your quirks are fake. The false self is the part that tries to exist on its own terms, apart from God, and needs everyone's applause to feel real. Third, the true self.
For Merton, it's who you are before God: known, loved, and given your being as a gift.

teach.h: HIDDEN IN THE LOVE OF GOD.
teach.b: He says the secret of who we are is hidden in the love and mercy of God. You don't build it. You find it, and receive it.
Saint Paul says something close, in the Douay-Rheims: "your life is hid with Christ in God." Fourth, why it's a relief.
When Samuel comes to anoint a king and passes over David's taller brothers, God tells him, in the Douay-Rheims: "for man seeth those things that appear, but the Lord beholdeth the heart."

teach.h: YOUR LIFE IS HID WITH CHRIST IN GOD.
teach.b: The world sees the bandages. The text says God sees the heart. For Merton, that's the relief: the true self doesn't depend on keeping the image perfect.

how: Catholics often explore the true self in spiritual direction and in the daily examination of conscience, and Merton's idea of the false and true self comes up in retreats and contemplative prayer groups.

o: the best version of you, built by hard work
who you are before God, beneath image and applause
your real personality, finally expressed freely

games.q: false and true — tap the pairs.
p: hidden in the love of God

s: Merton says your personality and talents are the false self
the false self is the part that tries to exist apart from God and lives on applause.
for Merton, you build your true self through achievement
you find it and receive it: it's hidden in the love and mercy of God.
Paul writes that your life is hid with Christ in God

games.q: Samuel comes to choose a king from Jesse's sons. the tall, impressive ones pass by first. what does God tell him?
o: man sees what appears, but the Lord beholds the heart
games.why: God passes over the impressive brothers and chooses David, the youngest, out with the sheep.

practice: Think of one small pretense you keep up, nothing dramatic: acting busier than you are, laughing at something that isn't funny, hiding that you don't understand.
See it clearly, without shame, then imagine setting it down for a moment and being looked at anyway, kindly; what's left is still you. If you pray, you can rest there, known.

wordCard.voice: True self. For Merton, who you are before God, known and loved, underneath the image and the applause. You find it; you don't build it. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: who god sees. Not the image, and not the applause. Day two hundred seventy-eight, done.

sources.q: your life is hid with Christ in God.

sources.ref: Thomas Merton, New Seeds of Contemplation (1961), chapters 5–7
